newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves German interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves German interest rates unchanged.

text.p: Germany's central bank said on Thursday its policy-making council had kept three key interest rates unchanged, largely meeting expectations that a string of weak economic data would not prompt a policy change.

The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank also said it had fixed its main money market rate at three percent for the next two weeks.
Economists had not expected any change in credit policy at the meeting, particularly after several Bundesbank council members said recently they saw no need to change credit costs any time soon.
Even news that German unemployment surged to a record level in January was judged by analysts as unlikely to prompt the tough Bundesbank into a policy move.
"The Bundesbank is not going to react like Pavlov's dog and adjust interest rates merely on the back of a few bad numbers," said Armin Kayser, economist at SBC Warburg in Frankfurt.
Germany's jobless rate surged to 12.2 percent from 10.8 percent in December, exceeding analyst's projections that the number of unemployed would exceed 4.5 million people.
The number now stands at 4.66 million people.
The sharp rise in unemployment follows weaker than expected December manufacturing orders, which showed a 1.4 percent drop and were released on Wednesday.
Ongoing sluggish economic conditions have refanned some speculation that the Bundesbank may ease interest rates once more in the current cycle.
But others believe the next move will be a tightening, which they say is unlikely to take place until the year-end at the earliest.
